parsed.summary: The Lean theorem proves three facts about the specific regular tetrahedron K = {(x,y,√2 t) : 0≤t≤1, |x|≤1−t, |y|≤t}. First, the infimum of its orthogonal shadow areas equals √2. Second, there exist δ>0 and C>0 such that for every 0<ε<δ there is a covering of K by exactly 2⌈2/ε²⌉ cylinders with nondegenerate triangular perpendicular bases, whose total area satisfies |Σ|B_i|/√2 − (1/2 − 13ε²/6000)| ≤ Cε⁴ and is strictly less than A_min/2. Third, some finite such covering of K has Σ|B_i|/|π_{u_i⊥}K| < 1/2. The main caveat is that Corollary 1.2 (every nondegenerate tetrahedron) is formalized only for this one regular tetrahedron, and Theorem 1.1's explicit range ε ≤ 1/2000 and constant 2 are replaced by existential δ and C.

glossary.plain: z ↦ z − ⟨u,z⟩u, the orthogonal projection onto u⊥ when |u|=1.
toReal of the 2-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure of a set in ℝ³.
glossary.note: This matches area only if Mathlib's euclideanHausdorffMeasure is normalized to agree with Lebesgue measure on planes. The conjunct A_min = √2 pins the normalization, so an unnormalized measure would make the theorem unprovable rather than vacuous.

glossary.standard_concept: A_min(K) = min over 2-planes E of |π_E K|
glossary.note: Lean uses an infimum and does not assert that the minimum is attained. The set is nonempty and bounded below by 0, so sInf is genuine.

glossary.plain: A unit axis u and a nondegenerate triangle B (convex hull of 3 affinely independent points) contained in u⊥. The compact, convex, measurable and finite-area fields are redundant consequences.
glossary.standard_concept: cylinder with compact triangular perpendicular base

glossary.note: Defined only for K, not for a general tetrahedron T.

glossary.plain: There exist δ,C>0 such that for all 0<ε<δ there is a covering by 2n(ε) triangular cylinders with |total/H − (1/2 − 13ε²/6000)| ≤ Cε⁴ and total < A_min/2.
glossary.note: δ and C are existential, whereas the paper gives ε ≤ 1/2000 and C = 2.

glossary.plain: Some finite triangular-cylinder covering of K has relative cost < 1/2.
glossary.note: Covers only K, not every nondegenerate tetrahedron.

lean_claims.plain: (i) inf_{|u|=1} |π_{u⊥}K| = √2. (ii) There exist δ>0 and C>0 such that for every ε with 0<ε<δ there are 2⌈2/ε²⌉ cylinders with unit axes and nondegenerate triangular bases in u_i⊥ covering K, with |Σ|B_i|/√2 − (1/2 − 13ε²/6000)| ≤ Cε⁴ and Σ|B_i| < A_min/2. (iii) There is a finite covering of K by such cylinders with Σ|B_i|/|π_{u_i⊥}K| < 1/2.

paper_claims.plain: A_min(K)=√2. For every 0<ε≤1/2000 there is a covering by m=2⌈2/ε²⌉ cylinders with compact triangular perpendicular bases such that (1/√2)Σ|B_i| = 1/2 − 13ε²/6000 + R with |R| ≤ 2ε⁴, and Σ|B_i| < A_min(K)/2.
A_min(K) = H, with equality attained at u=(1,0,0).
Every nondegenerate tetrahedron T admits a finite cylinder covering with compact triangular perpendicular bases with Σ|B_i|/|π_{u_i⊥}T| < 1/2.

coverage.why: The range of ε (any δ instead of 1/2000) and the constant (any C instead of 2) are existential; the cylinder count, leading terms and strict saving match.
Lean states the infimum value only, not that it is attained.
Lean covers only the specific regular tetrahedron K; the affine-invariance extension to all tetrahedra is not formalized.

flags.explanation: The corollary claims the counterexample for every nondegenerate tetrahedron. Lean proves it only for K, where it follows directly from part (ii) and A_min = H. The affine-invariance step is not formalized.

flags.explanation: The paper asserts the construction for every 0<ε≤1/2000 with remainder at most 2ε⁴. Lean only asserts existence of some δ>0 and C>0, so the explicit range and constant are lost.
flags.probe_idea: Replace ∃ δ C with δ = 1/2000 (using ε ≤ δ) and C = 2.

flags.explanation: Area uses Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure 2. This equals planar Lebesgue area only if that measure is normalized. Since A_min = √2 is proved, an unnormalized measure would have made the theorem false, so this is likely fine but worth confirming.
flags.probe_idea: Prove area of the unit square {(x,y,0) : x,y ∈ [0,1]} equals 1.

flags.explanation: A_min is an infimum; attainment of the minimum (the paper's 'min', equality at u=(1,0,0)) is not asserted.

lint_verdicts.why: The set is nonempty (unit vectors exist) and bounded below by 0 because areas are toReal values, so sInf is the true infimum.
Axes are unit vectors, so shadowArea ≥ A_min = √2 > 0 by part (i); the denominator is never zero.
n is only used with ε > 0.
2/ε² > 0, so the ceiling into ℕ matches ⌈2/ε²⌉.
H = √2 ≠ 0 and the literals are real.
This is division by 2 in ℝ.
